blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Two armies on two hills with a valley in between. Every morning and every evening, a champion came out of the Philistine camp. His name was Goliath. Six cubits and a span tall, taller than any man on either side, covered in armor head to toe.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He hollered across that valley, daring Israel to send one man to fight him. Forty days of that. Forty days, and nobody went.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then a shepherd boy named David came to camp, carrying food to his big brothers. He heard the giant talking. And he wanted to know why anybody should be allowed to defy the armies of the living God.

verses.text: And David said to Saul, Let no man’s heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.

segments.speaker: david
segments.text: Let no man’s heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.

verses.text: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.

segments.speaker: saul
segments.text: Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Saul was not wrong about the facts. David was young. Goliath was trained. But David had some facts of his own. He told the king how he kept his father's sheep, and how a lion came, and a bear came, and each one took a lamb, and he went after them and brought that lamb back.

verses.text: David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and the LORD be with thee.

segments.speaker: david
segments.text: The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Saul said unto David, Go, and the LORD be with thee.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: So Saul put his own armor on David, a helmet of brass and a coat of mail. David tried to walk in it and could not. He took it off. Church, you cannot fight your battle in somebody else's armor.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: David picked up his staff. He picked five smooth stones from the brook and dropped them in his shepherd's bag. His sling was in his hand.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The giant looked at him and sneered. Just a youth, ruddy in the face. And he cursed David by his gods.

verses.text: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then said David to the Philistine,

segments.speaker: david
segments.text: Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.

verses.text: And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD’s, and he will give you into our hands.

segments.speaker: david
segments.text: And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD’s, and he will give you into our hands.

verses.text: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When I say whose battle is it, you say, the LORD's. Whose battle is it? [PAUSE 3s | screen: "The LORD’s"] The LORD's. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "Whose battle is it?"] That is what David told the giant.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: One stone. And the giant fell on his face to the earth. David had no sword in his hand that day. He had a sling, a stone, and a God he had already met out on the hillside with the sheep.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Our grandmothers used to say, the giants don't get smaller, baby, your God gets bigger in your eyes. The story does not promise every battle ends like this one. It shows us where David's courage came from: the LORD who had been with him before.

pastor.note: Faithful to 1 Samuel 17; says outright the story does not promise every battle ends this way.

cultural.note: The saying is given to 'our grandmothers', the community, not an invented person.
